newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS- T-bond vols slip as U.S. stocks recover.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS- T-bond vols slip as U.S. stocks recover.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options edged back Monday as the stock market rebounded from Friday's 247-point drop in the Dow industrial average.
Fear of extended U.S. asset selling this morning boosted bond volatilities at the outset, but as U.S. stocks regained their footing, bond volatility was slightly deflated, options traders said.
"They were expecting the worst, and when that didn't happen, it eased," one bond options broker said of volatility.

Volatility for October options, which moved into the front-month position Sunday night, slipped to 8.65 percent by session's end from 8.85 percent at the opening, according to one trading desk. It closed Friday at about 8.75 percent.
With just one week to trade before they expire, September options saw volatility whip around through the session, finally settling at about 8.35 percent, down from 9.60 percent on the open.

Market participants said the day's activity was a mixed bag of position-squaring involving both puts and calls before Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting and speculative plays that featured selling out-of-the-money calls and buying low-delta puts.
September saw the bulk of the action, though most trades comprised 500 lots or less, traders said.

While the Fed is widely expected to take no action at Tuesday's policy meeting, thoughts that U.S. asset markets could be in for more wild swings this week inspired some traders to take on low-cost speculative positions in soon-to-expire September, said a second bond options broker.
"It could be a good week to be long gamma," said the first broker.
At the short end, Eurodollar volatilities were firm at 9.0 percent in December and 11.5 percent in March.
